questions.question_text:
Calculate the area of the isosceles triangle $ABC$.
The equal sides are $25$ cm and the base $AC$ is $14$ cm.

options.why: Uses the height as the area or omits the base factor in the triangle area formula.
Uses half the base times an incorrect height or misses the full altitude calculation.
Multiplies the side lengths or treats the triangle as having height 25 cm.

questions.solution_text: The altitude bisects the base, giving a right triangle with hypotenuse $25$ and base $7$. Its height is $\sqrt{25^2-7^2}=\sqrt{576}=24$ cm. Thus the area is $\frac12\times14\times24=168$ cm$^2$.
